claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically identifies hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in student essays.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: GPTZero's citation checker identifies fabricated references instantly to help educators maintain academic integrity.
claims.evidence_span: Our citation checker identifies these hallucinated references instantly, helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.

claims.claim_text: GPTZero source finder detects checkable objective claims in text and matches them to sources from online and academic data.
claims.evidence_span: Source finder will detect as many checkable, objective claims in your text and match those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines.

claims.claim_text: An artificial intelligence hallucination is a response generated by AI containing false or misleading information presented as fact.
claims.evidence_span: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), a hallucination or artificial hallucination (also called bullshitting, confabulation, delusion, or mirage) is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.

claims.claim_text: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.
claims.evidence_span: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.

claims.claim_text: The Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination in 2023 to include this new sense specific to the field of AI.
claims.evidence_span: In 2023, the Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination to include this new sense specific to the field of AI.

claims.claim_text: The survey provides an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.
claims.evidence_span: The present survey aims to provide an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations refer to statements made by the system which are either factually incorrect, illogical, or not substantiated by any credible sources.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations refer to statements made by the system which are either factually incorrect, illogical, or not substantiated by any credible sources but sound coherent and fluent on the face of it.

claims.claim_text: The survey reviews widely used benchmark datasets, evaluation frameworks, and emerging multi-layer verification architectures for improving AI trustworthiness.
claims.evidence_span: The survey further reviews widely used benchmark datasets, evaluation frameworks, and emerging multi-layer verification architectures for improving AI trustworthiness.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.

claims.claim_text: Hallucinations can be reduced but not fully eliminated, making them an active research problem for engineers.
claims.evidence_span: They can be reduced but not fully eliminated.

claims.claim_text: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.
claims.evidence_span: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.

claims.claim_text: An AI hallucination occurs when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.
claims.evidence_span: An AI hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.

claims.claim_text: Stanford research found that specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17 percent and 34 percent of the time.
claims.evidence_span: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.

claims.claim_text: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval Augmented Generation, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and guardrails led to a 96 percent reduction in hallucinations.
claims.evidence_span: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
